extra.message: req.body.username and req.body.password are passed directly into a Mongoose User.find() query without type enforcement. body-parser JSON is enabled in app.js, so an attacker can send {"username":"admin@snyk.io","password":{"$gt":""}} to satisfy the query and bypass authentication entirely.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: adminLoginSuccess() passes the attacker-controlled redirectPage value (req.body.redirectPage, set at line 41) directly to res.redirect() with no allow-list. This allows an open redirect that can send a freshly authenticated user to an arbitrary external site for phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: redirectPage is emitted with the unescaped EJS tag <%- redirectPage %> inside a value attribute. It originates from req.query.redirectPage (routes/index.js:71), so GET /login?redirectPage="><script>alert(1)</script> reflects attacker script into the response.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: The URL captured from user-supplied todo content (req.body.content, matched by imgRegex at lines 156-158) is concatenated into a shell command: exec('identify ' + url). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. a URL ending in "; touch ./public/p0wned") to execute arbitrary OS commands as the server user.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command (OS Command Injection)

extra.message: An uploaded ZIP archive (req.files.importFile) is extracted with AdmZip.extractAllTo('/tmp/extracted_files', true) without validating entry names. A malicious archive containing ../ path segments writes files outside the extraction directory (Zip Slip), enabling arbitrary file overwrite and potentially code execution.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: _.merge(message, req.body.message, {...}) recursively merges fully attacker-controlled JSON (lodash 4.17.4) into an object. A message payload containing {"__proto__": {"canDelete": true}} pollutes Object.prototype, letting an unprivileged user gain the canDelete permission used by the DELETE /chat handler.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes (Prototype Pollution)

extra.message: req.body.address is assigned verbatim to the user object and then passed to repo.save() (line 36). TypeORM performs an unsafe recursive merge, so an address value such as {"__proto__":{"where":{"id":"2","where":null}}} pollutes the prototype. The poisoned 'where' then overrides the hard-coded id filter in GET /users (line 16), allowing other users' records to be read.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes (Prototype Pollution)

extra.message: The /users router is mounted in app.js:69 with no authentication or authorization middleware. Both GET /users (line 8) and POST /users (line 26) are reachable anonymously; the source comment at lines 13-15 admits auth is not implemented, so unauthenticated callers can read and create user records.

The request body directly controls the persisted role field (user.role = req.body.role). Because POST /users is unauthenticated, a caller can create an account with role 'admin', escalating privileges.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes (Mass Assignment)

extra.message: A hardcoded application secret/token ('SECRET_TOKEN_f8ed84e8f41e4146403dd4a6bbcea5e418d23a9') is embedded in source code. Anyone with source access can reuse this secret.

The express-session secret is hardcoded to the well-known value 'keyboard cat'. An attacker who knows this secret can forge a signed connect.sid cookie containing loggedIn=1 and fully bypass the isLoggedIn authorization check on /admin and /account_details.
Database credentials are hardcoded in source: MySQL username 'root' and password 'root' (lines 11-12). This exposes privileged database access to anyone with the source.
The seeded administrator account is created with a hardcoded password 'SuperSecretPassword', giving a predictable default admin credential.

The device value from req.query.device (routes/index.js:304) is interpolated into the Dust {@if cond="'{device}'=='Desktop'"} expression. Dust 2.5.0 evaluates conditions with eval() and does not escape array inputs, so ?device[]=Desktop'-require('child_process').exec('...')-' achieves remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code (Eval Injection)

extra.message: Todo content is rendered with the unescaped output tag <%- marked(new String(todo.content)) %>. Although marked.setOptions({sanitize:true}) is set (app.js:75), marked 0.3.5's sanitizer is bypassable (e.g. [Gotcha](javascript&#58this;alert(1))), so attacker-stored todo content executes as script when the list is viewed.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: The created todo's Buffer content is returned base64-encoded to the client: res.status(302).send(todo.content.toString('base64')). With mongoose 4.2.4, storing a non-string value (e.g. {"content":800}) can cause uninitialized process memory to be included in the Buffer and leaked to the caller.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The hardcoded secret token is written to the application log via console.log('token: ' + token), disclosing the secret to anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: User-controlled todo content is passed to hms(time) (and later ms(period) at line 146). A long crafted duration string triggers catastrophic backtracking in humanize-ms/ms, blocking the Node.js event loop and causing denial of service.
